title: Symphony No. 9
hook: Mahler’s last finished symphony ends with music that slowly dies away into silence.

painting.title: Small Tree in Late Autumn
painting.pairingNote: Painted in 1911, the year Mahler died and a year before this symphony was first heard in Vienna, a bare young tree holding on alone against an empty sky.

facts: Mahler worked on the Ninth in the summer of 1909 at Toblach, in the Tyrolean mountains, where he had his last composing hut. It is the last symphony he completed.
He never heard it. Bruno Walter conducted the first performance in Vienna on 26 June 1912, a year after Mahler’s death.

It is often heard as a farewell: Mahler had lost his young daughter in 1907 and had been told he had a heart condition. Yet while writing it he was busy and planning ahead, so the farewell may be the listener’s as much as the composer’s.
An unusual shape: the first and last movements are slow, the middle two fast. It begins in D major and ends a semitone lower, in D-flat major, as if the ground had sunk.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a farewell to the world (I), clumsy country dances (II), defiance and fury (III), a hymn that fades into silence (IV).

movements.heading: Andante comodo
movements.title: Andante comodo
movements.summary: A slow movement that keeps breaking into violence. A gentle, sighing melody tries again and again to sing, and each time it is overwhelmed. Alban Berg called it the most glorious movement Mahler wrote, full of love for the earth.

mainIdeas.name: The limp
mainIdeas.description: an uneven, hesitating rhythm in the cellos and horn.

mainIdeas.name: The sigh
mainIdeas.description: a falling two-note phrase in the second violins, the main theme.

mainIdeas.name: The bell
mainIdeas.description: four notes tolled on the harp.

stops.hear: Cellos and a horn in a halting, uneven rhythm; a harp tolls
stops.happening: Leonard Bernstein heard Mahler’s irregular heartbeat in this rhythm

stops.hear: Second violins sing a falling two-note phrase, softly, in D major
stops.happening: The main theme, a gentle farewell

stops.hear: The music darkens into the minor; brass and strings become agitated
A swelling climax, then it breaks off
Sudden violence, marked “with fury”
Trombones and tuba blast out the halting rhythm “with greatest force”
A slow procession: timpani and deep bells toll the harp’s four notes
The opening rhythm and the sighing theme, quieter now
Flute, piccolo, oboe and solo violin answer each other like birds
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. Berg called this passage a vision of the hereafter

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: A high flute, a soft horn, a few plucked notes

movements.heading: Im Tempo eines gemächlichen Ländlers
movements.title: Im Tempo eines gemächlichen Ländlers
movements.summary: Three country dances, each faster and coarser than the last. Mahler marks the first one “somewhat clumsy and very coarse”. The dances are distorted until they almost stop being dances.

stops.hear: Bassoons and violas stomp out a heavy-footed dance
A faster, brasher waltz takes over
A slower, gentler dance; the sighing two-note phrase from the first movement returns
The waltz again, wilder and more grotesque
stops.happening: The dances start to fall apart

stops.hear: The clumsy first dance returns
The dances break into fragments

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: A tiny, cheeky phrase from piccolo and contrabassoon

movements.heading: Rondo-Burleske
movements.title: Rondo-Burleske. Allegro assai. Sehr trotzig.
movements.summary: Mahler’s angriest music, marked “very defiant”. A dense, snarling [[rondo|rondo]] full of [[fugue|fugue]] writing. In the middle, a moment of tenderness that the final movement will take up.

stops.hear: A trumpet snarls; strings and winds pile in, each with a different line
stops.happening: The defiant main theme, treated as a fugue

stops.hear: A cheap, swaggering tune
Dense counterpoint, voices crowding each other
The noise drops away. A trumpet sings a slow, tender phrase with a little turn
stops.happening: The middle episode. This phrase becomes the Adagio’s theme

stops.hear: Clarinets mock the tender phrase
The snarling music returns in full
Faster and faster
stops.happening: A headlong rush to a crashing end

movements.heading: Adagio
movements.title: Adagio. Sehr langsam und noch zurückhaltend.
movements.summary: A long hymn for strings, marked “very slowly and holding back even more”. It grows to a great climax, then thins out, phrase by phrase, until almost nothing is left.

stops.hear: Violins alone with a rising phrase, then the full strings in a deep, warm hymn
stops.happening: The main theme, built on the turn from the Rondo-Burleske

stops.hear: The texture empties: high violins and a low bassoon, far apart
The hymn returns, richer, with horns
Thin and bare again, almost motionless
The hymn begins to build
The whole string section strains upwards at full power
The hymn again, quieter, more broken
Strings alone, slower and slower, in fragments; the violins quote a phrase from Mahler’s *Kindertotenlieder* (Songs on the Death of Children)

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The strings hold the turn one last time; the sound fades to nothing
stops.happening: The last note is marked “ersterbend” (dying away)

notice: Do not reach for the next track when the music seems to stop. The final minutes are mostly silence, and the silence is part of the piece.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Barbirolli was famously thorough with Mahler: his first performance of the Ninth took nearly fifty hours of rehearsal. He worked regularly with the Berlin Philharmonic from 1961, and made this recording with them in January 1964.

threads.title: The sinking key
threads.body: D major at the start, D-flat major at the end: the symphony ends a semitone lower than it began.

threads.title: The turn
threads.body: A small ornamental figure, sung by the trumpet in the Rondo-Burleske, becomes the heart of the Adagio.

threads.title: Breaking off
threads.body: In every movement the music builds and then falls apart, until in the last pages it simply stops.
